extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners working on computational humor and text classification
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating models that predict whether a joke (from corpora such as Reddit, Short Jokes, or Pun of the Day) is humorous. Covers dataset construction/labeling, model choice (Transformer/BERT), training, baselines, and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor labeling cutoff (Reddit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Reddit upvote score distribution to label jokes as funny or not: the authors identified a major jump between the 0-200 upvote range and 200+ and used this natural divide as the cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cutoff produced 13,884 not-funny jokes and 2,025 funny jokes. The choice is data-driven (based on observed score distribution) but is audience-specific to Reddit r/Jokes and may not generalize to other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset variants (body, punchline, full)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create separate datasets for the body of the joke only, the punchline only, and a combined full (body + punchline) version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run experiments on each variant to determine which part of a joke carries more predictive signal; the paper found models and humans relied more on the punchline for humor prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative sample matching for Short Jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing non-joke (negative) samples for the Short Jokes dataset, extract sentences from a news crawl that match the jokes' word and character distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matching avoids trivial distributional cues between positive and negative examples, making classification rely on content rather than length/format differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train/validation/test split and stratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Split datasets into a 75/25 percent split, stratifying by labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratification preserves class proportions across splits; authors then applied up/downsampling steps described for training and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle class imbalance via upsampling (training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upsample the minority (humorous) class in the training set until it reaches an even 50% share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps the model learn despite an uneven amount of non-humorous jokes. Use only on training; validation and test are handled separately to maintain evaluation integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance validation/test via downsampling for interpretable accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Downsample validation and test sets into a 50/50 class split so that accuracy is balanced and easily understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balanced test sets ensure that accuracy isn’t dominated by the majority class; consider reporting metrics beyond accuracy for unbalanced real-world distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model choice: pre-trained BERT Transformer
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pre-trained BERT (multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder) as the base model and fine-tune with an additional output layer for the humor classification task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified by BERT's ability to recognize and attend to important words in sentence/paragraph contexts; self-attention layers can extract crucial features for humor detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training hyperparameters and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected hyperparameters include learning rate = 2e-05, max sequence length = 128, training up to 7 epochs, and creating checkpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the authors' chosen values; use checkpointing to select best model and monitor overfitting. Hyperparameters may need tuning per dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baselines for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Use previous strong models such as a CNN with Highway Layers (and variants like Word2Vec+HCF) and human performance as baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including both model baselines and human performance allows assessment relative to past automated approaches and to human-level judgment (general population vs Reddit users).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human baseline methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect human judgments via Mechanical Turk: 199 unique participants rated ~30 jokes each using prompts (context provided for body/punchline-only examples); use majority vote to compute human labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designing prompts that clarify context (e.g., 'Below is the punchline ...') yields comparable human labels; majority vote yields a consensus label for comparison against dataset labels and model predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score for model evaluation, matching metrics used in prior work (e.g., Chen and Soo 2018) for comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all four metrics, especially on balanced test splits; for imbalanced real-world data consider also reporting class-wise metrics, ROC/AUC, and calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer evaluation without fine-tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate a model trained on one dataset (Reddit) directly on other humor identification datasets (Short Jokes, Puns) without additional fine-tuning to test transfer capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tests generalization of learned humor features across datasets; for datasets with balanced labels (Short Jokes, Puns) no up/downsampling was applied during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of body vs punchline contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare model performance on body-only vs punchline-only datasets to infer which part of a joke carries more weight for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors observed higher reliance on punchline across models and humans; consider this when designing features or architectures that weigh punchline information more heavily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: audience-specific humor and subjectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that humor is subjective and that labels drawn from a specific community (Reddit r/Jokes) reflect that community's tastes; models may learn audience-specific humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret high accuracy as modeling a target audience's preferences rather than absolute truth; when deploying models consider the target audience and potential domain shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative reporting and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare new method results to prior work (e.g., CNN variants) using the same metrics and datasets to demonstrate improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present tables of Accuracy/Precision/Recall/F1 across methods and datasets; quantify improvements (e.g., Transformer achieved 0.931 F1 on Puns, 0.986 on Short Jokes) and discuss possible reasons (self-attention features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data/code for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Release code and datasets publicly to enable reproducibility and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors made their code and datasets open source; releasing data and code is recommended for evaluation transparency and fair comparison.
